ria: Quick note from a stress run: when the onboarding sample rotates tokens under load we saw a compressed retry burst and a handful of duplicated creates.

cho: Timeline? sounds like retries aligned after refresh.

ria: Short trace:
```
12:30:01 outgoing id=alpha auth=tok_old -> 401
12:30:01 onAuthRefresh started
12:30:01 onAuthRefresh done -> tok_new
12:30:01 SDK retries immediately (no jitter) -> upstream 429
12:30:01 retry state reset -> retried again quickly -> duplicate created
```

henry: Looks like the retry scheduler is being reset on auth success. If many clients refresh at once that becomes a retry storm.

cho: Which SDK? we've had parity differences historically.

ria: This repro used the JS quickstart wrapper. Py/Go kept attempt_count, JS rebuilt state, zeroing attempts.

henry: Short fixes I'd push: 1) keep RetryState across onAuthRefresh (parity), 2) add tiny random delay before immediate post-refresh retry (eg 40	60ms), 3) recommend Idempotency-Key header for create flows in the quickstart README.

cho: Also add a CI harness: simulate 60100 clients rotating tokens and assert duplicates <1%.

ops-bot: CI job scheduled: branch "devex/keep-retrystate-jitter" will run in staging at 2026-06-20T03:00Z.

ria: I'll file a ticket with the trace and repro script and include suggested patches + README note.

henry: I'll add a unit test in JS asserting attempt_count/next_delay unchanged after a fake onAuthRefresh. Put the jitter behind a flag so we can tune quickly.

cho: Also, add a short telemetry metric (privacy-safe) for cases where refresh happens within 1s of a retry and upstream returns 429 so we can measure how widespread this is.

ria: Filed: https://redwood-internal/issues/INFR-9012. Marking P2. Will follow up after the staging run.

henry: Thanks 44d will watch CI and run the 100-client overnight once deployed.
